angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 361,764 km at 179.88 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.5592 +/- 0.0984 mas (same row, RUWE 6.02): 179.88 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.52 +/- 0.038 solar radii from Torres et al. 2015, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-438 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...800...99T/abstract): 361,764 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.544 +/- 0.041 solar masses from Torres et al. 2015, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-438 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...800...99T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3748 +/- 112 K from Torres et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-438 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...800...99T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Torres et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-438 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...800...99T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-438.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.742, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
